text:
Like horrible batrachians toward the atmosphere,

lugubrious grimaces rise to the lip.

Through the blue Sahara of Substance

a gray verse walks, a dromedary.


A pout of cruel dreams phosphoresces.

And the blind man who died filled with voices

of snow. And to rise early, poet, nomad,

to the rawest day of being man.


The Hours go feverish, and in the angles

blond centuries of fortune miscarry.

Who pulls the thread so much: who lowers

without pity our nerves,

cords already worn, to the tomb!


Love! And you too. Black stones

are begotten in your mask and break it.

The tomb is still

a woman's sex that draws man on!

translation.title: Naked in Clay
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Vallejo's fierce surreal imagery: batrachians, Substance, worn nerves, and the erotic tomb.
